blocks.h: Two sources (teacher-written summaries of evidence, not quotations)

panels.title: Source A: summary of evidence given to a parliamentary committee in 1832
panels.text: A former mill worker told the committee that, as a child, he worked from about six in the morning until seven or eight at night, with short breaks. He said children who fell asleep or worked slowly were sometimes beaten by overseers, and that many were injured by machines.

panels.title: Source B: summary of a mill owner's evidence to an inquiry in the 1830s
panels.text: A mill owner said the children in his mill were well treated, did light work and were healthy and cheerful. He argued that limiting their hours would harm families who needed the wages and would make British cotton too expensive to sell abroad.

questions.q: Extend: Compare men's and women's experiences of industrial work.
questions.a: Similar long hours and danger; women paid less and often also ran homes

questions.q: Stretch: Why did reform take so long?
questions.a: Owners' influence in Parliament, belief in free markets, families needing wages

questions.q: The 1842 Mines Act banned underground work for:
questions.a: B) Women and boys under 10. It stopped women and girls, and boys under 10, working underground.

questions.q: Big question: better or worse than the land?
questions.a: Mixed: regular wages and town life, but longer hours, danger and less freedom
